trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or the RENFE R2 Nord train (€4.60) to the city center. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Drop off luggage and take a short stroll along Barceloneta beach promenade to decompress — the beachfront is lively even late at night in August.

meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack near the hotel — try a local 24-hour convenience store or a nearby chiringuito (beach bar) still open late. Budget €5–8 for a bocadillo (sandwich) and a drink.

day_by_day.notes: August nights in Barcelona are warm (~24°C/75°F), so the beach walk is very pleasant. Keep your belongings secure at the airport and on public transport — pickpocketing is common in tourist areas. Get a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) the next morning for budget transport all week.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, start the day with a walk along Barceloneta Beach (free). Head to the nearby Barceloneta Market (Mercat de la Barceloneta) to pick up fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee for a cheap breakfast. Then walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for a self-guided walking tour. Explore the narrow medieval streets, visit the Plaça Reial (free), and admire the exterior of the Barcelona Cathedral (free to enter early morning before 12:30).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the El Born neighborhood to see the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, small donation appreciated) — a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture. Wander through El Born's charming streets. Head to Parc de la Ciutadella (free entry) for a relaxing afternoon — rent a rowboat on the lake for ~€6/person or simply enjoy the monumental cascade fountain and lush gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Barceloneta waterfront area. Watch the sunset from the beach (free). Head to the nearby Port Olímpic area for Barcelona's famous nightlife scene — many bars offer free entry and cheap drink specials before midnight. Try a local beach bar for drinks and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from Barceloneta Market — fresh fruit, a croissant, and coffee. Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant in El Born — typically includes starter, main, dessert, bread, and a drink for €10–13. Look for spots away from the main tourist drag.
meals.dinner: Grab pintxos (Basque-style tapas) at one of the many pintxos bars in El Born — pieces typically cost €1.50–2.50 each. Budget €10–12 for a satisfying dinner with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter and El Born are very walkable from each other. Wear comfortable shoes — cobblestones are uneven. The menú del día is the best budget dining hack in Barcelona and is only available at lunch (Monday–Friday, sometimes weekends).

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to Barcelona's most iconic architecture. Take the metro to the Sagrada Família — book tickets online in advance (€26 for basic entry, €36 with towers — splurge if budget allows, or admire the exterior for free from Plaça de Gaudí). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring. Afterward, walk through the Eixample neighborhood to spot Gaudí's Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — the exteriors are free to admire and incredibly photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or bus to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a ticket (€10 — book online to save time), but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free and offer stunning panoramic views of Barcelona. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring. On the way back, walk down through the Gràcia neighborhood — a bohemian village-within-a-city with charming squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia where locals hang out.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Gràcia for the evening. The neighborhood has a fantastic local bar scene that's much cheaper than tourist-heavy areas. Join locals at a terrace bar in one of the plazas — order a clara (beer with lemon soda, ~€2.50) or local vermouth. Later, if you want more nightlife, head to the Eixample's 'Gayxample' area or Carrer del Consell de Cent for lively bars with no cover charge.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local bakery (forn de pa) in Eixample for a coffee and a croissant de mantequilla or a pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato). Budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Sagrada Família or in Gràcia — budget €11–13. Alternatively, grab a falafel wrap or a bocadillo from a local shop for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Vermutería or tapas bar in Gràcia — order patatas bravas (€4), pan con tomate (€3), and croquetas (€4–5). Full dinner with drinks for ~€12–15.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days in advance — they sell out fast in August. The Sagrada Família ticket is the biggest single expense of the trip but is considered unmissable. If skipping the interior, the exterior from the park across the street is still breathtaking and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Montjuïc hill. Walk or take the Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€12.70 round trip) or the cheaper Funicular de Montjuïc (included in metro T-Casual card). Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for sweeping views over the city and port. Explore the castle grounds and ramparts. Nearby, the Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic de Barcelona (€3.50) are beautiful and peaceful in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Fundació Joan Miró on Montjuïc (€14 entry — worthwhile for architecture and art lovers, or skip if very budget-tight and enjoy the free outdoor sculptures). Walk down the hill toward Poble Sec neighborhood — one of Barcelona's most up-and-coming and affordable areas. Explore Carrer de Blai, famous for its pintxos bars (great for a late afternoon snack). Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (€5) — a landmark of modernist architecture and often overlooked by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec and nearby Sant Antoni are Barcelona's hippest nightlife neighborhoods with great value. Start the evening at Mercat de Sant Antoni (free to browse, closes around 20:30) — a beautifully restored modernista market building. Then bar-hop along Carrer del Parlament and Carrer de Tamarit in Sant Antoni. Many bars have happy hours until 21:00. For a bigger night out, clubs in Barcelona don't get going until 01:00–02:00 — entry is often free before 01:00 with a drink included.

meals.breakfast: Café and tostada con tomate y aceite at a local bar near the hotel or metro stop. Budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in Poble Sec — the neighborhood has excellent value restaurants. Budget €10–12.
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai — grab 4–6 pintxos and a drink for €10–14. This street is famous for cheap, delicious Basque-style bites.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (~30°C/86°F) — Montjuïc is exposed, so bring water and sunscreen. The Funicular is the most budget-friendly way up the hill. Poble Sec and Sant Antoni are safe, local neighborhoods — a great escape from the tourist crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow morning at Barceloneta Beach — take a final swim in the Mediterranean (free). Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade. Visit the nearby Parc de la Barceloneta or explore the sculpture 'Rebecca' and Frank Gehry's iconic golden 'Peix' (Fish) sculpture near the Hotel Arts — great photo opportunities for free. Stop at the Barceloneta neighborhood's interior streets for an authentic local feel — far less touristy than the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Las Ramblas for a final stroll (stay alert for pickpockets). Visit La Boqueria Market (Mercat de Sant Josep) — even if prices are tourist-inflated, it's a feast for the eyes. Buy a fresh juice (€1.50–2 from inner stalls) rather than prepared food for better value. Walk to the nearby MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona) — the building's architecture by Richard Meier is stunning and the plaza in front is a famous skateboarding spot. Entry is €12 or free on the last Sunday of the month. Explore the El Raval neighborhood around it — gritty, multicultural, and authentic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, pack up, and enjoy a final dinner near the beachfront. Take time to watch the sunset over the Mediterranean one last time. Depending on departure time, enjoy a farewell drink at a beachfront bar. Head to the airport via Aerobus or RENFE train.

meals.breakfast: Fresh churros and hot chocolate at a local café or grab yogurt and fruit from a nearby supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl for best prices). Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: La Boqueria fresh juice and a bocadillo, or a cheap menú del día in El Raval. Budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Farewell paella or arrós negre (black rice) at a mid-range restaurant in Barceloneta — look for set menus around €15–18. Avoid restaurants with aggressive touts on the beachfront; walk one block inland for better prices and quality.

day_by_day.notes: Keep track of checkout time at Aegean Bliss Resort — most hotels allow luggage storage after checkout if your flight is in the evening. La Boqueria is best visited early morning on weekdays to avoid the worst crowds. Budget summary for the trip: transport ~€25, main attraction tickets ~€55–65, food ~€15/day = approximately €130–160 total for 5 days excluding accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Focus on transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Allow 45–60 minutes for baggage claim, customs, and taxi or Aerobus transfer to the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — still in transit or preparing for arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort around 23:30–00:00. Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxing stroll along the nearby Barceloneta beachfront promenade to decompress after the flight. Grab a light late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour chiringuito (beach bar) or hotel bar before heading to bed.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the hotel bar or a nearby Barceloneta beach bar — try a simple bocadillo (sandwich) or patatas bravas. Budget ~€10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Barcelona nightlife runs late so resist the temptation to go out — save your energy for the full days ahead. Set an alarm and prepare comfortable walking shoes for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café on Barceloneta beach. Then head to the Sagrada Família Guided Tour (pre-booked skip-the-line tickets essential in August). Spend 2–2.5 hours marveling at Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica, exploring both the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring interior forest of columns, and the museum in the crypt. Book the first morning slot (~9:00–9:30 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to the Gràcia neighborhood for lunch. Then head uphill to Park Güell for the Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration. Explore the colorful mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the panoramic views over Barcelona. Stroll through the charming Gràcia neighborhood streets on the way back, popping into local boutiques and plazas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a quick refresh, then head to El Born neighborhood for the Tapas Crawl & Vermouth Experience. Start with a classic vermouth at a traditional bar, then hop between 3–4 tapas spots sampling patatas bravas, croquetas, pan con tomate, and fresh seafood pintxos. El Born is easily accessible from the Beachfront area.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or hotel breakfast — croissant, coffee, and fresh orange juice. Budget ~€6–10.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in Gràcia neighborhood — try La Pepita or a local menú del día (set lunch menu with starter, main, dessert, and drink) for ~€12–15.
meals.dinner: Tapas crawl in El Born — budget ~€25–35 per person across multiple stops including drinks. Try Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet for a classic experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets online at least 2–3 weeks in advance for August — they sell out fast. Park Güell's Monumental Zone also requires timed-entry tickets (~€10). Wear sunscreen and comfortable shoes — this is a high-walking day.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Gothic Quarter Walking Tour. Spend 2–2.5 hours wandering through Barcelona's medieval labyrinthine streets, discovering Roman ruins (Temple d'August), the stunning Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards. A guided small-group tour is ideal for context and storytelling. The Gothic Quarter is a short walk or taxi from the Beachfront hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-tour, have lunch in the El Born area, then spend a free afternoon exploring the Picasso Museum (budget ~€12 entry) and the beautiful Santa Maria del Mar Gothic church nearby. Browse the boutique shops and art galleries of El Born at a relaxed pace. Alternatively, return to the hotel for a beach afternoon at Barceloneta — swim, sunbathe, and recharge for the big night ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight is the Nightlife Tour: Clubs & Rooftop Bars. Begin with sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Raval or the Barceloneta area (~8:00–9:30 PM). Move on to a cocktail bar in El Born around 10:00 PM, then hit one of Barcelona's legendary clubs — Pacha, Opium, or Shôko on the beachfront — after midnight. Barcelona nightlife doesn't peak until 1:00–2:00 AM.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery — pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and coffee. Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: El Born casual lunch — try El Xampanyet or a local bocadillo bar. Budget ~€12–18.
meals.dinner: Pre-nightlife dinner at a mid-range restaurant in El Raval or Barceloneta — try fresh seafood paella or fideuà. Budget ~€20–30. Eat late (9:00–10:00 PM) to align with local rhythm.

day_by_day.notes: For the nightlife tour, book rooftop bar reservations in advance (Mirablau, La Isabela, or Hotel Arts Sky Bar are excellent options). Clubs typically charge €15–25 entry with one drink included. Dress smart-casual. Carry a small crossbody bag and keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter and nightlife areas.

day_by_day.morning: A slower start after the late night — sleep in until 9:00–10:00 AM. Enjoy a proper sit-down brunch near the hotel on Barceloneta beach. Then take a leisurely walk along the Port Olímpic waterfront. Visit the Barceloneta Market (Mercat de la Barceloneta) for a glimpse of local life and fresh produce. Optionally, rent a bike along the beachfront path for a scenic coastal ride toward the Forum area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or taxi up to Passeig de Gràcia — Barcelona's grand architectural boulevard — for a self-guided architecture walk. Admire the three iconic Modernista buildings: Casa Batlló (exterior or interior tour, ~€25–35), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera (the 'Block of Discord'). Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop tour (~€22–25) offering stunning views and Gaudí's extraordinary chimney sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening back near the Beachfront. Have dinner at a mid-range seafood restaurant in Barceloneta, then take an evening walk along the illuminated beachfront promenade. For a quieter nightcap, visit a rooftop bar at one of the nearby beach hotels for cocktails with sea views — a more relaxed alternative to the previous night's clubbing.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at La Cova Fumada area or a beach café — eggs, toast, fresh juice. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Quick bite on Passeig de Gràcia — a café or a bocadillo from a local deli. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner in Barceloneta — try La Mar Salada or La Cova Fumada for fresh grilled fish, gambas al ajillo, and local white wine. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló and La Pedrera both require advance booking in August. Consider the Magic Nights at La Pedrera rooftop event if available — it's a memorable evening experience with live jazz. The Passeig de Gràcia walk is best done in the late afternoon when the light is softer and temperatures drop slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Barcelona — enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel or a favorite café discovered during the trip. Spend the morning on Barceloneta beach for a last swim and sunbathe session. Browse the beachfront souvenir shops for gifts. Pack and check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 12:00 PM — arrange late checkout if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before departure, visit Montjuïc Hill via cable car or bus for panoramic views over Barcelona, the port, and the sea. Explore the Montjuïc Castle briefly and stroll through the gardens. Alternatively, revisit a favorite neighborhood for last-minute shopping — El Born for artisan gifts or Passeig de Gràcia for mid-range fashion and design stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special mid-range restaurant — treat yourself to a proper Catalan meal with escalivada, botifarra sausage, or a classic crema catalana dessert. Head to the airport or arrange onward transport. Barcelona El Prat Airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the Beachfront area by taxi (~€30–35) or Aerobus (~€6).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a café on the beach — full spread with coffee, pastries, and fruit. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Montjuïc or a packed picnic from a local market — olives, cheese, cured meats, and bread. Budget ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner at a mid-range restaurant in El Born or Barceloneta — try Espai Mescladís or Bodega Sepúlveda for an authentic experience. Budget ~€30–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and allow extra time for August airport queues — arrive at El Prat at least 2.5 hours before departure. Store luggage at the hotel or a luggage storage service (Stasher or Bounce) if checkout is earlier than your flight. Barcelona's August heat peaks in the afternoon (30–35°C expected) — stay hydrated and carry water throughout all days.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early luggage drop-off service if available. Keep the first night light — Barcelona's energy starts tomorrow. Set an alarm for a relaxed but purposeful Day 2 start.

Skip-the-line access included — a private or small-group guide will walk you through Gaudí's extraordinary unfinished basilica, explaining the symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave interior, and the towers offering panoramic city views. Stop at a local café for a cortado and pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up. Dinner at a top-tier restaurant — recommended: Lasarte (3 Michelin stars, modern Basque-Catalan cuisine) or Disfrutar (avant-garde tasting menu, consistently ranked among the world's best). meals.lunch: Light lunch in Gràcia neighborhood — recommended: La Pepita or a local pintxos bar for premium bites without a heavy sit-down meal.
meals.dinner: Lasarte (Carrer de Mallorca, 259) or Disfrutar (Carrer de Villarroel, 163) — luxury tasting menus with wine pairings. Budget €150–€250 per person.

day_by_day.afternoon: Transition from history to indulgence: embark on the Tapas Crawl & Vermouth Experience through El Born and La Barceloneta — both easily walkable from the Gothic Quarter and your hotel. Sample traditional tapas: patatas bravas, croquetes de jamón, boquerones, gambas al ajillo, and locally crafted vermouths. El Born's gourmet food scene and proximity to the beach make this an ideal premium afternoon food journey.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary Nightlife Tour: Clubs & Rooftop Bars. Begin with sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Raval or Eixample (recommended: Hotel Arts Sky Bar or Paradiso cocktail bar for pre-drinks). Then move on to Barcelona's premier clubs — Pacha Barcelona, Opium, or Otto Zutz — for a world-class nightlife experience. VIP table reservations recommended.

meals.lunch: Tapas Crawl through El Born and La Barceloneta — budget €40–€70 per person across multiple stops including vermouth, pintxos, and small plates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega 1900 (Albert Adrià's vermouth bar and modern tavern, Carrer de Tamarit, 91) — elevated traditional Catalan cuisine in a stunning modernista setting. Budget €80–€120 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Gothic Quarter walking tour — cobblestones can be uneven. The nightlife scene in Barcelona starts late; clubs don't fill until midnight or 1am. Then explore the Eixample district independently: walk the iconic grid-patterned streets and admire the concentration of modernista masterpieces — Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Palau del Baró de Quadras. day_by_day.afternoon: Private architectural photography walk through Eixample and Passeig de Gràcia — hire a professional photographer or guide to capture the trip in style. Afterward, treat yourself to a premium spa afternoon at the Aegean Bliss Resort — massage, hydrotherapy, and relaxation ahead of another big evening. Alternatively, visit Palau de la Música Catalana (a UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall) for a guided tour of its breathtaking stained-glass interior.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel's rooftop terrace with Mediterranean views. Then, private table dinner at Angle Barcelona (1 Michelin star, modern Catalan cuisine by Jordi Cruz) or Alkimia (innovative Catalan fine dining).
